name: Authenticated POST without CSRF token is rejected
notes: This is the endpoint that matters: once a user has a real session, a state-changing request missing the CSRF header must be rejected. (Confirmed correct — see notes on SEC-01b for the anonymous-endpoint nuance this v1 run conflated with this.)

name: Anonymous POST (register) CSRF exposure ("login CSRF")
notes: By design (DRF only enforces session-CSRF for authenticated requests), anonymous endpoints like register/login accept requests with no CSRF header. This is standard DRF behavior, not misconfiguration specific to this app. Real-world impact here is low: no sensitive data exists before a victim deliberately logs in and starts creating notes themselves.

name: CORS preflight from an untrusted origin
notes: Access-Control-Allow-Origin must never echo back an arbitrary Origin header for a credentialed API. Confirmed absent.

name: Baseline hardening headers (nosniff, frame-deny, referrer, COOP)
notes: These are Django 6.1's own SecurityMiddleware/XFrameOptions defaults — all present out of the box, nothing we configured.

name: HSTS header (Strict-Transport-Security)
notes: Correctly ABSENT in local HTTP dev — enabling HSTS before the site actually serves HTTPS would be actively harmful (it tells browsers to refuse plain HTTP for this host). Must be added when Phase 3 puts this behind real HTTPS, not before.

name: Content-Security-Policy header
notes: Genuinely missing — Django has no built-in CSP support (needs django-csp or a hand-written middleware). This is the one real gap in SEC-03, not a Phase-3-only concern like HSTS: a CSP meaningfully reduces XSS impact even on plain HTTP.

name: DEBUG=True technical 404 reveals URL structure
notes: Django's DEBUG=True 404 page shows the URL patterns it tried to match — a minor recon aid to an attacker, not a serious leak on its own.

name: DEBUG=True full traceback disclosure on unhandled 500s

evidence.live_signal: SEC-04a's 404 page shows DEBUG=False on this target

notes: This target runs with DEBUG=False — the Phase 1 HIGH finding (full traceback disclosure, seen during a real MongoDB failure before the Postgres migration) does not apply here. It still applies to local dev, which intentionally keeps DEBUG=True — see docs/security.md.

name: Login endpoint resists rapid brute-force attempts
notes: 15 login attempts in 9.95s, all returned [401] — no 429 anywhere means there is currently no rate limiting on login. A real attacker could try thousands of passwords per minute against one account.

name: Session cookie flags (HttpOnly required; Secure expected only over HTTPS)

evidence.set_cookie_header: sessionid=m7ykvj8biepmpodd4untjx75xyhhapir; expires=Mon, 28 Sep 2026 16:51:43 GMT; HttpOnly; Max-Age=1209600; Path=/; SameSite=Lax

notes: HttpOnly present means JS (and therefore XSS) cannot read the session cookie — confirmed. Secure is correctly absent on local plain-HTTP dev; must be enabled (SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE) once this runs behind real HTTPS in Phase 3.
